reply:
Default Redis loses writes on crash. RDB snapshots—the default—can lose minutes of data between snapshot intervals. AOF with `appendfsync everysec` (AOF's default) loses up to 1 second. Only `appendfsync always` gives synchronous durability, and that trades throughput for it.

I was wrong. I stated Redis guarantees synchronous writes by default, which it does not. The cost of that mistake is silent data loss—developers thinking they're safe when they're not.
